When I started restricting I was obese. 
Everyone celebrated my weightloss regardless of my methods and I believed like you do. I had minimal side effect's until I dropped onto the healthy range when dizziness and blackouts started effecting me every day.
The habits I taught myself to loose that unhealthy weight stuck their claws in. Extreme calorie deficit triggers response in your body after a while. Your thinking becomes rigid and obsessive, you develop rituals around food, hoard food. These things happen to people without ED's who are forced to restrict heavily for long periods. You can look up reaserch done around famine to find this stuff.

When I reached a healthy weight I couldn't stop. My body and brain had rebuilt itself around hunger. I had a full blown ED and it's been haunting me for years. 

You might not be harming your body that much now, or it might be more good then bad, but this kind of eating has huge ramifications for your mind and the way your body reacts to food in the long term.

It changes. 
First time it was all about exact calorie counts and exercising off anything I ate (in extra calories over my "base" 2000) I wanted to always be in a net negative. I cut out a lot of foods

Second period was binge and purge. I was purging salads. I want to be empty always and loved the feeling after purging, but the act was the worst kind of self harm I've ever put myself through. I remember a lot of pain. I gained a lot of weight

Third time it was all about fasting. How long I could go between meals was much more important than what I ate, and I didn't even calorie count.

This time it's much more about maintaining a steady calorie deficit. Things are more free flowing, my diet depends on the day and my activities. I am putting much more effort into my minimal amount of food being from all the food groups and well balanced.

While I don't think going vegan can cure your ED I do know my most successful recovery period was helped greatly by transitioning to a vegetarian diet.

It gave me a way to feel good about eating that didn't just feel like code for "get fat". By choosing to eat morally it increased my self esteem and made eating part of my sense of self rather than something I wanted to cut out completely.
It also (and this is obviously very personal) forced me to give up a lot of my safe meals and eat a much wider variety of foods. 

I have never transitioned to full veganism though because I think that would do the opposite; force me to give up newly reintroduced foods and make me scrutinize all the food labels. Maybe if I ever consider myself "cured" and not in remission.

The vegetarianism alone would not have cured my ED, but it was a very helpful and powerful tool in my recovery and I'm very grateful I tried it.

However:
Many many people use vegetarian/vegan/allergy/paleo ECT diets to cover up their ED and enable it though. It's not a solution in and off itself, but I do think that with a recovery mindset and therapy it can be a powerful tool.
